The error shown is the Cloudflare message 'The origin web server sent a response that Cloudflare could not parse... empty response, malformed HTTP headers, or an otherwise invalid response' (HTTP 520).

integration_issues.flow: Caller rapid navigation: Leads -> lead detail /leads/600027 while loading -> Leads -> Follow-ups -> WhatsApp -> Leads
integration_issues.issue: Previous-route GETs are aborted, but at least some canceled promises are unhandled, so navigation does not complete cleanly and the user sees an error overlay instead of the final page data.

action_items: Fix all route-mounted async GET flows that can be aborted so ERR_CANCELED is always caught/ignored, especially FollowUps.jsx load()/counts and WhatsAppInbox.jsx loadChannels()/polling.
Retest the exact caller rapid path after the fix: Leads -> /leads/600027 -> Leads -> Follow-ups -> WhatsApp -> Leads, verifying no runtime overlay/toast and final Leads data loads.
Consider a broader grep for useEffect async API.get calls without catch so RouteChangeAborter cannot create any unhandled canceled promise on navigation.
critical_code_review_comments: The fix guarded Dashboard.jsx, Leads.jsx, and LeadDetail.jsx top-level load catches, but the reported route sequence also hits FollowUps.jsx and WhatsAppInbox.jsx. FollowUps.jsx calls async load() from useEffect without catch and has a counts IIFE without cancel handling; WhatsAppInbox.jsx calls async loadChannels() from useEffect/interval without catch. Aborting these GETs can still reject as CanceledError.

App.js adds a window unhandledrejection guard for ERR_CANCELED, but runtime evidence shows it did not prevent the React dev error overlay from displaying CanceledError during rapid navigation in preview.

rca_of_the_issue: The client now aborts previous-route GETs on pathname changes, but not every page in the affected route sequence handles canceled promise rejections. FollowUps.jsx and WhatsAppInbox.jsx contain async API.get flows invoked from useEffect/interval without catch around aborted calls. Those cancellations surface as unhandled CanceledError runtime errors, recreating the user's 'move between tabs while loading => error/hang' symptom in preview.
